official.deadline_note: MEXT publishes only the cycle rhythm, not a central date: 'Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next April is made between April and May of the previous year. First screening is conducted between May and August by the Japanese Embassies or Consulates General.' The binding deadline is the one set by the embassy or consulate general in the applicant's country of nationality.
official.application_cycle: FY2027 intake (arrival April 2027); recruitment April-May 2026, embassy first screening May-August 2026, final results notified after February 2027.
official.status_note: MEXT published the FY2027 Application Guidelines for students arriving in Japan in April 2027; recruitment for that intake ran in April-May 2026, so the next annual cycle is the live target.
official.tuition_coverage_note: FY2027 guidelines, section 7: 'Education Fees: Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities will be waived.'
benefits: Supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the accepting university
One year of preparatory Japanese language education at ABK College (humanities/social sciences) or Osaka University (natural sciences) where applicable
Round-trip airfare: economy-class ticket to Japan and a return ticket on graduation
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible
In principle born on or after 2 April 2002 (under 25 years of age)
Completed 12 years of schooling, or a school equivalent to a Japanese upper secondary school, or passed an academic qualification examination equivalent to 12 years of schooling
Able to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027
Willing to study in Japanese and to deepen understanding of Japan
In good physical and mental health, evidenced by a physician-signed certificate in the prescribed format

Write the document number from 1 to 9 in the upper right corner of the first page of each document
All written academic examination subjects are taken by every applicant

Certificate of enrollment, if currently enrolled at a university
selection_criteria: First screening by the Japanese diplomatic mission: document review, written academic examinations and an interview
Written examination subjects: Japanese, English, mathematics and science
Second screening by MEXT, which selects candidates from each course
Direct placement without preparatory education is available for applicants with sufficient Japanese ability, mainly in Social Sciences and Humanities
coverage: Tuition, matriculation and entrance examination fees exempted at the accepting national university
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided under embassy recommendation
One year of preparatory education where applicable
application_method: Embassy recommendation: submit the full packet to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of nationality by the deadline that mission sets
University recommendation: apply to a Japanese university that holds an MEXT recommendation quota; that university submits the recommendation to MEXT
official.application_route: Two official routes: embassy recommendation (packet to your Japanese diplomatic mission) or university recommendation (a quota-holding Japanese university nominates you).
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants select a field of study on the Field of Study sheet; examination subjects depend on the chosen field (science-faculty applicants choose two of chemistry, physics or biology).
official.duration: 5 years including one year of Japanese language training at ABK College or Osaka University; 7 years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and 6-year pharmacy; up to a standard school year under university recommendation
official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 funds international students who will study at Japanese national universities as undergraduates, with terms published in the FY2027 Application Guidelines. The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition at the accepting university and provides round-trip airfare; under embassy recommendation the scholarship runs for five years including one year of Japanese language training.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
official.english_requirement: The official MEXT scholarship page lists the First Screening written examination subjects for undergraduate students as Japanese, English, mathematics and science (science-faculty examinees choose two of chemistry, physics or biology). MEXT sets no separate TOEFL or IELTS score, and language proficiency certificates are optional supporting documents.

applicant_utility.summary: MEXT's undergraduate award covers the full package a student in Japan needs: JPY 117,000 a month, no tuition or entrance fees, paid economy flights both ways, and a preparatory year of Japanese before your degree starts. Two routes exist - embassy recommendation through your own Japanese diplomatic mission, or university recommendation through a quota-holding Japanese university - and the route you pick changes who screens you first. Whichever you choose, the fixed 1-7 April 2027 arrival window and the embassy's own document deadline are the two dates to build your year around.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers under 25 who want a fully funded undergraduate degree in Japan and can demonstrate strong Japanese, English, mathematics and science examination results.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your Japanese embassy or consulate general for the current guidelines and note its internal submission deadline
Decide between embassy and university recommendation early; if pursuing university recommendation, verify the target university holds an MEXT quota
Prepare original and copy packets with documents numbered 1-9 in the top right corner
Book the physician-signed medical certificate on MEXT's prescribed form well in advance
Confirm you can be in Japan between 1 and 7 April 2027 before applying
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy's own deadline while looking for a central MEXT date that does not exist
Weak written examination results; every applicant sits all subjects, including science-faculty candidates taking two sciences
Submitting files with untranslated documents or missing the second copy packet
Being unable to arrive in the fixed early-April window, which cancels travel support
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, baggage costs, and personal spending during the first weeks before the allowance starts.
document_audit: Transcripts must show the grading scale used, and graduation or prospective-graduation certificates must be current
The recommendation letter should come from a school president, dean or academic advisor
Thesis abstracts are requested only if applicable; language certificates only if held
The Direct Placement Preference Form is a post-first-screening document, not part of the initial packet
alerts: Expect one year of preparatory Japanese education unless you are placed directly, which is mainly for Social Sciences and Humanities applicants with sufficient Japanese
Screening reasons are not disclosed and placement objections are not accepted
Medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and six-year pharmacy stretch the scholarship to seven years
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Obtain guidelines from the diplomatic mission, submit original plus copy packets by its deadline, sit the written examinations and interview, then await MEXT's second screening and university placement.

official.deadline_note: MEXT publishes only the cycle rhythm: 'Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next October is made between December of the previous year and the following February. The first screening is conducted between January and February by the Japanese embassies or consulates general.' The binding deadline is set by the diplomatic mission in the applicant's country.
official.application_cycle: 2026 edition (October 2026 arrival): recruitment December 2025 to February 2026, embassy first screening January to February 2026. The next edition follows the same December-February rhythm for an October 2027 arrival.
official.status_note: The 2026 edition guidelines cover students arriving in Japan in September/October 2026; recruitment for that edition ran December 2025 to February 2026, so the next edition is the live target.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 2026 guidelines, section 7: 'Education Fees: Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation and tuition at universities are waivered.'
benefits: Monthly scholarship of JPY 117,000 paid after arrival in Japan
Supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the designated university
One year of study at a designated Japanese university through the Japanese Studies Program
Round-trip airfare: economy-class ticket to Japan and back to the home country

Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible
Undergraduate at a university outside Japan majoring in a field related to the Japanese language and/or Japanese culture, still enrolled there on return
Has studied Japanese studies at university for a total of one year or more as of 1 September 2026
Japanese language ability sufficient to receive education at a Japanese university in Japan
Physician-signed health certificate confirming no condition hindering study in Japan
requirements: Submit the documents to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country by the designated deadline
Select preferred universities only from the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program and enter the course code

Write the document number from 1 to 8 in the upper right corner of the first page of each document

Document verifying at least one year of Japanese language and culture study, if not verifiable from the transcript
Recommendation letter (free format; a sample is provided)
Medical certificate in the prescribed FY2026 form
Certificate of Japanese language ability, if the applicant can supply proof
Photograph taken within six months, 4.5 x 3.5 cm, attached to the Application Form

Second screening by MEXT, which confirms the university placement
coverage: Tuition, matriculation and entrance examination fees exempted at the designated accepting university
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided under embassy recommendation
application_method: Embassy recommendation: submit the complete document set to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of nationality
University recommendation: applicants may also reach the programme through a Japanese university recommendation

official.application_route: Apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality (or via a Japanese university recommendation) for the Japanese Studies Program.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan and must be enrolled as an undergraduate at a university outside Japan, remaining enrolled there on return.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international undergraduates majoring in Japanese language or Japanese culture at universities outside Japan.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must major in a field related to the Japanese language and/or Japanese culture; those majoring in other fields pursuing complementary studies do not qualify.
official.duration: One year of study at a designated Japanese university through the Japanese Studies Program course listed in the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program
official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Japanese Studies Students funds international undergraduates who major in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year at designated Japanese universities. MEXT states it 'offers scholarships to international students who wish to study for a period of one year at designated Japanese universities as Japanese Studies Students'.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
official.english_requirement: MEXT sets no separate English test for this category: the official MEXT scholarship page lists the First Screening examination subject for Japanese studies students as Japanese. Applicants must have Japanese language ability sufficient to receive education at a Japanese university, and a Japanese language ability certificate is an optional supporting document.

applicant_utility.summary: If you are already an undergraduate majoring in Japanese language or culture outside Japan, this scholarship sends you to a designated Japanese university for one fully funded year: JPY 117,000 per month, no tuition, round-trip airfare, and your home-university enrolment preserved for your return. The screening leans heavily on Japanese - the written examination at the embassy is in Japanese, and you need enough Japanese to be taught at a Japanese university. Applications run December to February for an October arrival, so the practical window opens right after the autumn term starts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Current undergraduates aged 18-29 majoring in Japanese language or Japanese culture at a university outside Japan, with at least one year of Japanese studies completed.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will still be enrolled at your home university on return; this is a binding condition
Check that your total Japanese studies reach one year or more by the 1 September 2026 reference date in the guidelines
Pick preferred universities strictly from the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program and copy the course codes exactly
Ask your university for a certified transcript covering all academic years to date
Obtain the prescribed medical form signed by a physician and attach a recent 4.5 x 3.5 cm photograph to the application form
common_rejection_risks: Majoring in an unrelated field with Japanese as a complementary study, which does not qualify
Missing the December-February recruitment window for the October intake
Insufficient Japanese to receive education at a Japanese university or to pass the Japanese written examination
Losing home-university enrolment status, which ends eligibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the airport, airport taxes, travel insurance, baggage costs and personal spending beyond the monthly allowance.
document_audit: If the transcript does not clearly show one year of Japanese studies, add the separate verification document
The recommendation letter is free-format but a sample is provided; use it
The photograph must be under six months old and attached to the form
Number documents 1-8 in the upper right corner - one digit fewer than the undergraduate scheme
alerts: This is a one-year scholarship, not a degree programme; plan how the year fits your home degree
You must newly obtain a Student visa and enter Japan with Student residence status
Placement is at a designated university from the Course Guide, not a free choice of any Japanese university
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: During December-February, submit the full document set with placement preferences to your Japanese embassy, sit the Japanese written examination and interview there, then await MEXT's confirmation of your designated university.
